Hi Amy —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard and the immediate next steps so everyone is aligned. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- Current latency spikes when the model scales >100 concurrent sessions (p95 ~220–300ms) impacting clinician workflows.
- Regulatory requirement to keep PHI isolated and audited; your legal team prefers customer-dedicated compute for certain workloads.
- Predictable throughput for overnight batch scoring and daytime interactive queries (target ~600 reqs/min sustained, bursts to ~1.2k).

Goals you stated:
- Put a production-grade, HIPAA-ready inference path in place by end of Q1 2027.
- 99.9% availability target for core inference endpoints; 95th/99th latency objectives to be negotiated once we size pools.
- Minimize token/unit cost while preserving model parity with current on-prem.

What we propose (high-level):
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) with tenant isolation (no co-tenancy) for PHI workloads.
- Autoscaling buckets for sustained throughput + short burst capacity for morning load spikes.
- Optional Private deployment (VPC/IPsec) if you need fully customer-managed networking and HSM integration.
- SLA baseline: 99.9% availability with a per-route latency SLO framework (to be finalized during sizing).

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra team — propose Wed 12/09 or Thu 12/10; (owner: jasmine_liu)
2) Provide draft qualification checklist + security evidence (SOC2 artifacts, network diagram) — deliver by 12/07; (owner: jasmine_liu + security)
3) Pool sizing recommendation & cost ballpark after deep dive — deliver within 3 business days post-deep-dive; (owner: karthik_iyer)
4) Commercial sketch (commit/price buckets + burst policy) — initial draft by 12/08; (owner: ben_carter)

Attachments: MedCura-dedicated-sla-slides.pdf (slides); MedCura-qualification-checklist.xlsx (starter checklist).

If this aligns, I’ll lock the deep-dive for 12/09 11:00am PT and send calendar invites.

Thanks — quick technical reply ahead of the deep-dive: 

1) Warm vs cold: we can support a mixed strategy. Recommend keeping a small pool of warm nodes (sized to handle the 95th percentile of morning spike) and allow short-lived burst workers to spin up for larger surges. Warm nodes eliminate model kernel load time; bursts add 5–15s cold-start depending on model size.

2) Sizing suggestion (initial):
- Baseline reserved pool: 4 x A100-class equivalents for low-latency interactive (this targets ~600 reqs/min with headroom).
- Burst pool: ephemeral workers that can scale to additional 6 GPUs to cover peaks (~1.2k).
- KV-caching & request coalescing should be enabled to reduce token throughput; we will parameterize after seeing sample traffic.

3) Isolation options:
- Dedicated Redwood pool (single-tenant run-level) with network isolation and per-token audit logs — least friction.
- Private deployment (VPC + optional on-prem-like packaging) if MedCura requires full customer-controlled network + HSM. This adds lead time and a platform fee; discuss in commercial.

4) Azure/region: we can deploy in us-west (Azure) but will validate image/kernel compatibility and region capacity ahead of sizing. If Azure is constrained, our fallback is a colocated cloud region in us-west with equivalent SKUs; we’ll surface any failure modes in the deep-dive.

I’ll prepare a short ops memo and sample cost assumptions before 12/08. For the deep-dive let’s include: one infra engineer from MedCura, their security lead, and our ops engineer (I’ll bring a couple of slides on topology and cold-start mitigation).

– Karthik

Redwood Inference
